name: commit-corner
description: A visual Git client for VS Code: commit graph with staging, worktree and pull request review (GitHub.com), multi-commit diffs, files bold until viewed, line staging, blame, interactive rebase, stashes and worktrees. No runtime dependencies, no telemetry; network access is git itself plus, optionally, GitHub sign-in and the GitHub API for pull request details.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Commit Corner runs git, which can execute hooks and configured programs from the repository.

scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:vscode

commitCorner.gitPath.markdownDescription: Path to the git executable. Empty uses `git` from `PATH`.

commitCorner.repositoryScanDepth.markdownDescription: How many folder levels below each workspace folder to look for nested repositories (0 = only the workspace folders).

commitCorner.repositoryScanIgnoredFolder.markdownDescription: Folder names skipped when looking for nested repositories.

enumDescriptions: Ask before opening a repository outside the workspace (remembered per repository).
commitCorner.detectRepositoriesOfOpenFil.markdownDescription: Whether to open the git repository of a file you open from **outside** the workspace folders. Opening runs git there, which can run programs that the repository's own configuration names, so it asks first by default.

commitCorner.openRepositoryInParentFolde.markdownDescription: What to do with a repository found in a folder *above* a workspace folder (e.g. a dotfiles repo in your home directory).

enumDescriptions: Keep views up to date while VS Code is in the background, at most every few seconds (watching an agent or a terminal at work).
Refresh only when the window gets focus again.
commitCorner.refreshWhenUnfocused.markdownDescription: How views refresh while the VS Code window is not focused.

commitCorner.statusLimit.markdownDescription: Show at most this many changed files in Source Control (0 = no limit). Very large numbers usually mean a build folder is missing from .gitignore.

commitCorner.dateFormat.markdownDescription: How dates and ages are shown in the graph (editor and sidebar) and the commit and branch rows of the tree views. `relative` shows ages (`7h`, `3d`); hover cards and tooltips always add the full date.

commitCorner.ai.enabled.markdownDescription: Generated commit messages (the sparkle button, Generate Commit Message, in the graph's commit box and in Source Control) and summaries of changes (worktrees, pull requests, commits), written by a language model through VS Code's Language Model API — the provider you installed and signed in to, such as GitHub Copilot. Nothing is sent unless you ask; VS Code asks once before Commit Corner may use a model. What is sent: the diff you asked about (including the content of new, untracked files), file names, and — for commits — their messages, authors and dates; for a commit message also the branch name and the last 10 commit subjects. Files that may hold secrets (`.env`, keys, credentials…) are sent by name only and known token formats are removed (best effort). A user setting only: a workspace cannot turn it on.

commitCorner.ai.modelFamily.markdownDescription: The language model to use: its family, id or name (for example `gpt-4.1` or `claude-sonnet-4.5`), or pick one with **Commit Corner: Choose Language Model…**. Empty, or not available: the default model of GitHub Copilot, else any available model. When several providers offer it, Copilot's is used; Copilot CLI's models are skipped (they do not answer other extensions). Output → Commit Corner logs the model chosen and how it answered. A user setting only.

commitCorner.writeCommitGraph.markdownDescription: When a repository with 5,000 or more commits has no commit-graph file (git's index of the history, which `git gc` also writes), write it once in the background, 30 seconds after the repository opens. The graph and history views load much faster with it.

commitCorner.ai.includeUntracked.markdownDescription: Send the content of new, untracked files with the changes (a generated commit message when nothing is staged, a worktree summary). Off: new files are left out of what is sent (neither content nor names). A user setting only (a workspace cannot turn it on); `untrackedFiles: "no"` in your user settings also turns it off.

commitCorner.untrackedFiles.markdownDescription: How untracked files are listed: every file (`all`), only top-level untracked folders (`normal`), or not at all (`no`).

commitCorner.quickDiff.markdownDescription: Gutter change markers against the index. `auto` enables them only when the built-in Git extension is disabled, to avoid duplicate markers.

commitCorner.countBadge.markdownDescription: Number badge on the Source Control icon. `auto` shows it only when the built-in Git extension is disabled.

commitCorner.statusBar.markdownDescription: Branch and sync items in the status bar. `auto` shows them only when the built-in Git extension is disabled. The merge/rebase-in-progress indicator is always shown.

commitCorner.explorerDecorations.markdownDescription: Change badges and colours in the Explorer and editor tabs. `auto` enables them only when the built-in Git extension is disabled.

commitCorner.smartCommit.markdownDescription: What to do when committing with nothing staged.
enumDescriptions: Ask whether to stage everything first
Stage all changes (including untracked) and commit

commitCorner.protectedBranches.markdownDescription: Branch names (wildcards allowed, e.g. `release/*`) that ask for confirmation before you commit to them directly.

commitCorner.openConflictsIn.markdownDescription: Where clicking a conflicted file opens it.

commitCorner.checkoutNewBranch.markdownDescription: Check out branches right after creating them.

commitCorner.fetchAllRemotes.markdownDescription: Fetch from all remotes (`git fetch --all`) instead of only the default one.

commitCorner.pullRebase.markdownDescription: Pull with `--rebase` by default. When off, git's own `pull.rebase` setting applies.

commitCorner.pushFollowTags.markdownDescription: Push annotated tags that point at pushed commits (`--follow-tags`).

commitCorner.syncAlwaysPull.markdownDescription: Sync always pulls before pushing, even when the last fetch showed nothing new.

commitCorner.autoFetchMinutes.markdownDescription: Fetch all repositories every N minutes while the window is focused. 0 disables auto-fetch.

commitCorner.networkTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Cancel fetch, pull and push after this many seconds (0 = no limit; you can always cancel from the notification). Auto-fetch uses 120 seconds when this is 0.

commitCorner.askpass.markdownDescription: Ask for credentials (HTTPS username/password or token, SSH key passphrase, host key confirmation) in VS Code dialogs. Requires a window reload to change.

commitCorner.githubAuthentication.markdownDescription: When git asks for the credentials of an HTTPS **github.com** remote, use the GitHub account signed in to VS Code (Accounts menu; asked once). The same, already granted session is also used for pull request details from the GitHub API (`commitCorner.pullRequests.githubApi`). Background fetches and the API use it only when already signed in.

commitCorner.githubHostAliases.markdownDescription: SSH host aliases that stand for github.com (from `~/.ssh/config`, e.g. `github-work` in `git@github-work:org/repo.git`), so web links, permalinks and pull request details work for such remotes too.

commitCorner.graph.pageSize.markdownDescription: Commits loaded per page in the graph.

commitCorner.graph.showAuthor.markdownDescription: Show the author column in the graph.

commitCorner.graph.showDate.markdownDescription: Show the date column in the graph.

commitCorner.graph.showSha.markdownDescription: Show the commit column in the graph.

commitCorner.graph.showChanges.markdownDescription: Show the Changes column in the graph: lines added and deleted per commit, loaded for the rows on screen.

enumDescriptions: Branches stay together (each line of history in one piece).
Newest commit first, with Today / Yesterday / This week / This month / Older separators, like the sidebar.
commitCorner.graph.order.markdownDescription: Order of the graph in the editor tab. The sidebar Graph always lists by date.

commitCorner.fileLayout.markdownDescription: Show changed files as a folder tree or as a flat list in views.

commitCorner.showAuthorInLists.markdownDescription: Show the author next to commits in tree views.

commitCorner.avatars.markdownDescription: Show initials avatars (coloured per author, generated locally; nothing is downloaded) next to commits in the tree views.

commitCorner.treeStats.markdownDescription: Show lines added and deleted next to commits in the tree views. They load in the background after the list is shown.

commitCorner.branchSort.markdownDescription: Sort branches by most recent commit or by name.

commitCorner.branchCommitsLimit.markdownDescription: How many commits to list under an expanded branch.

commitCorner.fileHistoryLimit.markdownDescription: Commits loaded per page in File History.

commitCorner.timeSeparators.markdownDescription: Split commit lists in the tree views (File History, branches, Outgoing/Incoming, Compare, pull requests) into Today, Yesterday, This week, This month and Older, like the sidebar Graph.

commitCorner.sidebar.oneViewAtATime.markdownDescription: Show one Commit Corner view at a time in the sidebar (the Graph by default); switch with **☰ Graph** at the top of the Graph, the Switch View menu in each view's title bar or the Actions hub (`Ctrl+Alt+G Space`). VS Code cannot collapse a view for an extension, so the others are hidden, not collapsed. Off: all six views stack.

commitCorner.markUnviewedFiles.markdownDescription: Show files you have not viewed in **bold** (graph) or with a dot (tree views); a commit you started on counts what you have seen ("3/12"). Opening a file marks it viewed. Marks survive an amend or rebase that leaves a change as it was; an uncommitted file is bold again when its content changes.

commitCorner.pullRequests.listOnOpen.markdownDescription: List pull requests (one `git ls-remote`) automatically when the view is shown.

enumDescriptions: Titles, authors, state, reviews and checks from the GitHub REST API (api.github.com), with your VS Code GitHub sign-in when there is one; public repositories also work signed out.
Git only: pull requests are listed by number with `git ls-remote`.
commitCorner.pullRequests.githubApi.markdownDescription: Where the Pull Requests view gets pull request details from. Diffs always come from git (`refs/pull/*`).

commitCorner.blame.currentLine.markdownDescription: Show author, date and message at the end of the current line.

commitCorner.blame.statusBar.markdownDescription: Show the blame of the current line in the status bar.

commitCorner.blame.maxLength.markdownDescription: Maximum length of the current-line blame text.

commitCorner.blame.maxLines.markdownDescription: Do not blame files longer than this.

commitCorner.blame.ignoreWhitespace.markdownDescription: Ignore whitespace-only changes when blaming (`git blame -w`).

commitCorner.blame.detectMovedLines.markdownDescription: Follow lines moved or copied from other files (`git blame -C`). More accurate, noticeably slower on large histories.

commitCorner.blame.delayAfterEdit.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait after typing before blaming the unsaved text again.
